From c589e3ca27c9f608004b155d3acb2fab6f7a9f26 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Sep 2022 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] RISC-V: Avoid coupling the T-Head CMOs and Zicbom

We could make the T-Head CMOs depend on a new-enough assembler to have
Zicbom, but it's not strictly necessary because the T-Head CMOs
circumvent the assembler.

Fixes: 8f7e001e0325 ("RISC-V: Clean up the Zicbom block size probing")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220915170900.22685-1-palmer@rivosinc.com
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>

diff --git a/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h b/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h
index a89c005b4bbf..273ece6b622f 100644
--- a/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h
+++ b/arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h
@@ -42,8 +42,12 @@ void flush_icache_mm(struct mm_struct *mm, bool local);
 
 #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */
 
-#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZICBOM
+/*
+ * The T-Head CMO errata internally probe the CBOM block size, but otherwise
+ * don't depend on Zicbom.
+ */
 extern unsigned int riscv_cbom_block_size;
+#ifdef CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZICBOM
 void riscv_init_cbom_blocksize(void);
 #else
 static inline void riscv_init_cbom_blocksize(void) { }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/riscv/include/asm/cacheflush.h`**
   - A comment was added to clarify the relationship between the T-Head CMO errata and the Zicbom ISA. The comment states that the T-Head CMOs internally probe the CBOM block size but do not depend on Zicbom.
   - The `riscv_init_cbom_blocksize` function declaration is conditionally included based on the `CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZICBOM` configuration. If Zicbom is not enabled, a static inline version of the function is provided that does nothing.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications establish a clearer understanding of how the T-Head CMOs interact with the Zicbom ISA. By adding the comment, the patch clarifies that while the T-Head CMOs can probe the CBOM block size, they do not require Zicbom to function. This decoupling allows for more flexibility in the use of the T-Head CMOs without being strictly tied to the availability of the Zicbom feature in the assembler. The conditional function declaration further supports this by providing a no-op implementation when Zicbom is not configured, ensuring that the code remains functional regardless of the Zicbom configuration.

Here is the commit message:
RISC-V: Avoid coupling the T-Head CMOs and Zicbom

We could make the T-Head CMOs depend on a new-enough assembler to have
Zicbom, but it's not strictly necessary because the T-Head CMOs
circumvent the assembler.

Fixes: 8f7e001e0325 ("RISC-V: Clean up the Zicbom block size probing")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <lkp@intel.com>
Reported-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220915170900.22685-1-palmer@rivosinc.com
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>

Here is the root cause:
The T-Head CMOs were incorrectly coupled with the Zicbom ISA, leading to unnecessary dependencies that could cause issues if Zicbom was not available. This coupling could result in improper initialization or functionality of the T-Head CMOs when Zicbom was not configured, as they were designed to circumvent the assembler but still relied on its presence for certain operations.
